name: Ama Dablam Expedition
sub_region: Solukhumbu District, Koshi Province (Khumbu Himal, Sagarmatha National Park; base camp above Pangboche)

difficulty.technical_grade: AD+ to D (operator assessments); original 1961 line described as VI 5.9 60deg
difficulty.notes: Department of Tourism expedition peak, not an NMA trekking peak. Standard route is the Southwest Ridge: mixed rock, snow and ice on fixed ropes from Camp 1. Crux is the Yellow Tower (steep granite, jumar) just below Camp 2; Mushroom Ridge and snow flutes above Camp 3. Camp 2 is a cramped ridge ledge. Since a serac collapse above old Camp 3, many teams treat Camp 3 as a brief stop and summit from Camp 2. Prior technical (jumar, steep rock in crampons, ice axe) experience is expected; altitude is lower than an 8,000 m peak.

duration_days.notes: Most commercial programmes are 25 days (about 8 days approach Lukla-Base Camp, rotations and a summit window, 3-4 days out). Rapid/pre-acclimatised formats exist. Autumn is the main commercial season.

max_altitude_point: Ama Dablam summit (DoT royalty table 6,812 m; Himalayan Database 6,814 m)
start_point: Kathmandu (fly to Lukla, or via Manthali/Ramechhap in peak seasons)

itinerary.notes: Leave the EBC trail the next day.
Grassy meadow/moraine west of the ridge; operators also list 4,500-4,570 m. Puja.

itinerary.route: Skills, puja, and rotation: Yak Camp / ABC (about 5,200 m) - touch Camp 1 (about 5,700 m) - return to Base Camp
itinerary.notes: Fixed-line practice. Camp altitudes vary by year.

itinerary.route: Second rotation: sleep Camp 1; touch Camp 2 (about 5,900-6,100 m, above the Yellow Tower) - return to Base Camp
itinerary.notes: Yellow Tower is the technical crux.

itinerary.route: Rest, then summit window: Base Camp - Camp 1 - Camp 2 - Camp 3 (about 6,200-6,400 m, often not slept) - summit 6,812 m - descend
itinerary.walking_hours: Summit day from Camp 2 commonly pre-dawn; 40-50 degree snow/ice above Camp 3
itinerary.notes: Mushroom Ridge and hanging serac (the dablam) above. Weather buffers sit in this window.
Some teams helicopter from Base Camp.

best_seasons.notes: Autumn is the main commercial season (fixed ropes, more teams). Spring is climbed. DoT royalty is the same in spring and autumn (USD 1,000), unlike most other DoT peaks.

permits.name: Department of Tourism climbing royalty - Ama Dablam (6,812 m)
permits.fee: USD 1,000 per person spring (Mar-May) and autumn (Sep-Nov); USD 500 winter (Dec-Feb) and summer (Jun-Aug)
permits.status: VERIFIED (spring on DoT); autumn and winter/summer UNVERIFIED-minor per _regulations.json (operator copies of the gazette table)

permits.name: Garbage management deposit (refundable, per expedition team) - Khumbu/Annapurna schedule for Ama Dablam
Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person per entry (SAARC NPR 1,500)

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Trek-Card
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person (SAARC and Chinese nationals NPR 2,000)

permits.name: Seasonal rope-fixing fee
permits.fee: Operator quotes about USD 150-200 per climber
permits.applies_to: climbers on the commercial SW Ridge

guide_requirements: DoT expedition: registered Nepali agency; government liaison officer attached under the Tourism Act. Sixth Amendment (royalties from 1 Sept 2025): at least one mountain guide per team on peaks other than 8,000 m. Mandatory staff insurance minimums apply. Some 2026 operator pages still quote the obsolete NMA-style ~USD 400 royalty; Ama Dablam is not an NMA peak.

flights: Optional helicopter from Base Camp / Pangboche
drives: Kathmandu - Manthali about 4-5 h when Lukla flights are diverted
logistics.notes: Teahouses to Pangboche; tented Base Camp and high camps. Camp 2 tent sites are limited in busy October weeks. Supplemental oxygen is not standard on commercial Ama Dablam (unlike 8,000 m peaks).

highlights: Southwest Ridge, first climbed 13 March 1961 by Mike Gill, Wally Romanes, Barry Bishop and Mike Ward (Silver Hut / Hillary expedition; Hillary led the expedition, not the summit party)
Base camp meadow with Everest-Lhotse-Nuptse across the valley
risks: Fall and exposure on the Yellow Tower and ridge camps
Serac / hanging glacier (the dablam) above the upper route; Camp 3 serac history
Crowding and limited tent platforms at Camp 2 in autumn
Weather and wind on the summit snowfield

acclimatization.notes: Two rotations typical before the summit push; extra rest days at Base Camp between rotations.

unverified: DoT autumn/winter royalty figures: spring USD 1,000 is on the DoT page; autumn USD 1,000 and winter/summer USD 500 are from operator reproductions of the gazette (_regulations.json: UNVERIFIED-minor).
Summit height 6,812 m (DoT, Sagarmatha NP) vs 6,814 m (Himalayan Database, Nepal Himal Peak Profile) vs older 6,856 m maps.
Rope-fixing fee USD 150-200 per climber (single operator range).
Alpine grade AD+/D is operator language, not a DoT classification.
Whether TIMS is charged to expedition members (TAAN has stated TIMS is not required for mountaineering-permit holders).
